slides.texte_overlay:
How to become ridiculously
social in a new city
Become a regular somewhere. Same café, same gym, same time each week. The staff start greeting you by name, and regulars slowly turn into the first familiar faces in your new city.
Join something with a weekly meeting. A run club, a climbing gym, a pub quiz team. Seeing the same people every week does the hard work of friendship for you.
Say yes to every invitation in the first three months. Even the boring ones. You never know who you'll meet, and people stop inviting the guy who always says no.
Ask locals for their favourite spots. "Where do you go for the best coffee around here?" People love showing off their city, and it often turns into an invitation to come along.
Before: weekends alone in a city I didn't know. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a story about every street, which makes meeting people so much easier.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: weekends alone in a city I didn't know. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now meeting people feels so much easier.

slides.texte_overlay: Host something small. Invite three people from different places for pizza at yours. Mixing your new contacts turns scattered acquaintances into an actual group of friends.
Follow up within 48 hours. "Great meeting you at the quiz, want to join us next week?" Most people mean to follow up and never do. The guy who does ends up with a full calendar.
